title: The shell: what shows before anything streams

slides.say: When you stream HTML, there's a part React must finish first. It's called the shell.
The shell is everything outside any Suspense boundary. Here that's the layout and the cover, plus the big spinner fallback.

slides.text: The shell is the earliest loading state the user can see. Wrap the whole app in one Suspense, and the shell is just a spinner.
slides.say: The shell is the earliest loading state a user may see. If you wrap your entire app in one Suspense boundary, the shell is only a spinner. That feels slower.
On shell ready fires when the whole shell has rendered. That's usually when you start streaming, even though nested boundaries may still be loading.

slides.text: Aim for a shell that's minimal but complete, like a skeleton of the page layout.
slides.say: So place your boundaries to make the shell minimal but complete, like a skeleton of the whole page.
